title: JSON Parameter Authoring Guide and Contextual Error Guidance
creator: Alya Torres
description: Goal: Provide a single, pragmatic JSON schema definition pattern for function/tool parameters that balances strict validation for predictable runtime behavior with helpful, contextual error messages for SDK and Console UX. This ticket codifies the authoring conventions, validation modes, telemetry signals, and an error-code vocabulary. It also defines guidance for compatibility with legacy short-form parameter manifests.
spec_summary: 1) Canonical manifest shape: {name, description, params: [ {id, type, required, schema, examples, coercion_hint, deprecation_note} ], version, compatibility}. 2) Supported primitive and composite types: string, integer, number, boolean, enum, array<T>, object, uri, iso8601, base64. 3) Schema field is a JSON-schema-lite subset: type, min, max, pattern, format, enum, items, properties; no $ref or allOf/anyOf in primary manifest (see migration section). 4) Examples: include at least one valid and one invalid example to improve runtime error suggestions.
validation_behaviour: We propose three validation modes: strict, permissive, and adaptive. - strict: server rejects any non-conforming request with structured error (400+code). - permissive: server attempts coercion (string->number, parse booleans), logs telemetry and returns warnings in the response envelope. - adaptive: runtime learns common coercions per-customer for non-sensitive workloads and suggests manifest changes in Console. Mode is selectable at route or model binding level.
coercion_and_repair_rules: Coercion hints are explicit in the manifest. Server will only coerce when manifest includes coercion_hint for that field. Coercion precedence: numeric parsing, boolean synonyms (yes/no/true/false), date parsing (ISO fallback), base64 detection. If coercion fails but permissive mode is enabled, the system returns a typed warning and the original raw value to calling SDK for developer inspection.
error_code_vocabulary: We define a compact set of stable error codes that map to UX-level messages: - ERR_PARAM_MISSING - ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH - ERR_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE - ERR_PATTERN_MISMATCH - ERR_ENUM_MISMATCH - ERR_ARRAY_ITEM_INVALID - ERR_COERCION_FAILED - ERR_DEPRECATED_PARAM_USED - ERR_TOO_LARGE_PAYLOAD. Each error includes 'path' to field, 'expected' and 'received' strings, and a 'suggestion' free-text field.
error_message_guidance: Messages should be diagnostic and actionable. Example: 'ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH: path=/payment/amount expected=number received=string suggestion=Send a numeric value (e.g., 12.50) or enable coercion_hint in the manifest.' For UX consumption, the Console will translate codes into user-facing copy and surface inline fixes (toggle coercion, add example, mark required).
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit per-invocation metrics: validation.mode, validation.result (pass/warn/fail), error.code, coercion.applied (true/false), manifest.version, customer_id. Track rates of ERR_COERCION_FAILED and ERR_PARAM_MISSING for product alerts. Store sample failing payloads (scrubbed) for 30 days in Console diagnostics.
backcompat_and_migration: Support a legacy short-form parameters array where 'type' was a single string and constraints were encoded in 'hint' text. Migration path: automated translator in the authoring UI that suggests a canonical manifest with best-effort extraction. When migrating, preserve manifest.version and add a 'legacy_source' annotation string. Old manifests without explicit schema will default to permissive mode with telemetry flagging for author review.
acceptance_criteria: Authoring UI inserts canonical manifest template and validates locally before save
Runtime rejects strict-mode violations with documented error codes
Permissive mode returns warnings in response envelope and logs coercions
Console shows top 10 validation failure reasons per-route and links to example payloads
SDK surfaces structured error payload (code, path, suggestion) and preserves raw server response
test_plan: Unit tests: validate manifest parser and coercion engine (coverage > 90%)
Integration: end-to-end requests for strict/permissive/adaptive modes with synthetic payloads
Fuzzing: random payload generator to ensure graceful failure and no panics
Load: simulate burst of malformed requests and assert latency SLOs degrade minimally
Regression: run migration translator on 1k legacy manifests from customer staging data
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): enable strict mode only for internal testing routes and opt-in customers
Phase 2 (beta): surface authoring UI and migration translator to select customers; collect telemetry for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (general): enable permissive default for legacy manifests and make strict the default for newly created manifests
Rollback: revert to permissive default at route level; feature flag in control plane
migration_notes: Automated translator runs in the Console on save; it creates a draft canonical manifest and requires explicit author approval. For customers with >100 manifests we provide a bulk migration tool (dry-run mode recommended) and a support playbook.
